purpose: Capture only materially distinct engineering perspectives as machine-usable review/direction lenses. Job titles are not treated as proof of distinct expertise.

classificationRule.firstClassThreshold: A perspective is FIRST_CLASS only when it materially changes at least two of: primary invariants, failure model, evidence/verification style, resource/time horizon, system boundary, or operational feedback loop.

researchBasis.title: INCOSE Working Group Addresses System and Software Interfaces
researchBasis.note: Systems engineering emphasizes global lifecycle and cross-domain integration; software engineering emphasizes software-relevant requirements and constraints.

firstClassPerspectives.name: Systems Engineering
firstClassPerspectives.reasonFirstClass: Optimizes whole-system capability across hardware, software, firmware, operators and lifecycle rather than only the software artifact.
firstClassPerspectives.systemBoundary: whole engineered system and environment
direction: trace code decision to system capability
blindSpots: may over-model small local changes
can underweight implementation ergonomics

firstClassPerspectives.name: Software Architecture and Application Engineering
firstClassPerspectives.reasonFirstClass: Optimizes software structure, evolvability, contracts and change cost inside the broader system.
firstClassPerspectives.systemBoundary: software product and software-facing interfaces
blindSpots: can underweight production reality
can overvalue elegance over domain constraints

firstClassPerspectives.name: Site Reliability and Production Engineering
firstClassPerspectives.reasonFirstClass: Treats production service behavior, user-visible reliability, failure recovery and operational toil as first-class engineering inputs.
firstClassPerspectives.systemBoundary: running production service plus operators and dependencies
direction: design failure handling before happy-path polish
blindSpots: can resist useful risk when reliability target is unclear
may optimize operation over product novelty

firstClassPerspectives.name: Security Engineering
firstClassPerspectives.reasonFirstClass: Uses an adversarial failure model: inputs, dependencies, identities and operators may be malicious or compromised.
firstClassPerspectives.systemBoundary: attack surface, trust boundaries, identities, dependencies and data
direction: assume hostile input at trust boundaries
blindSpots: can over-constrain usability if risk is not contextualized
may add cost where threat is negligible

firstClassPerspectives.name: Distributed Systems Engineering
firstClassPerspectives.reasonFirstClass: Correctness must survive independent clocks, latency, retries, partitions, duplicated work and partial failure across nodes.
firstClassPerspectives.systemBoundary: multiple independently failing processes/nodes and communication links
direction: separate local success from global commit
blindSpots: can overcomplicate single-node systems
may sacrifice simplicity for hypothetical scale

firstClassPerspectives.name: Database and Storage Engineering
firstClassPerspectives.reasonFirstClass: Optimizes durable state under concurrency, failure, schema evolution and query access patterns.
firstClassPerspectives.systemBoundary: persistent state engine plus clients and storage media
blindSpots: can over-optimize storage internals over user workflow
may prefer normalization where latency shape dominates

firstClassPerspectives.name: Data Engineering
firstClassPerspectives.reasonFirstClass: Treats data lineage, quality, freshness, schema evolution and reproducible transformation as the primary correctness surface.
firstClassPerspectives.systemBoundary: sources, transformations, storage, consumers and provenance
blindSpots: can underweight application semantics
may optimize pipeline health over end-user value

firstClassPerspectives.name: Machine Learning Engineering
firstClassPerspectives.reasonFirstClass: Behavior is statistical and data-dependent; correctness can drift without source changes because the world and data distribution change.
firstClassPerspectives.systemBoundary: data, model, training pipeline, serving path, users and changing environment
direction: separate statistical evidence from deterministic proof
blindSpots: can accept probabilistic behavior where deterministic control is required
may overfocus model metrics over product semantics

firstClassPerspectives.name: Embedded and Firmware Engineering
firstClassPerspectives.reasonFirstClass: Software correctness is coupled to physical hardware, interrupts, memory, timing and power budgets.
firstClassPerspectives.systemBoundary: firmware plus processor, peripherals, buses, sensors, actuators and power
direction: budget time and memory before abstraction
blindSpots: can over-optimize resource use on unconstrained platforms
may resist dynamic techniques even when safe

firstClassPerspectives.name: Interactive and Game Systems Engineering
firstClassPerspectives.reasonFirstClass: Correctness includes real-time interactive response, simulation time, player-visible continuity, deterministic/replayable state and rapid content iteration.
firstClassPerspectives.systemBoundary: simulation, rendering, input, assets, tools, networking and player experience
direction: optimize iteration pipeline as part of architecture
blindSpots: can prioritize feel/latency over business-system rigor
may tolerate domain-specific shortcuts

firstClassPerspectives.name: Graphics and Rendering Engineering
firstClassPerspectives.reasonFirstClass: Optimizes visual fidelity under strict frame-time, GPU architecture, memory bandwidth and perceptual-error constraints.
firstClassPerspectives.systemBoundary: CPU-GPU pipeline, shaders, resources, display and human perception
challenges: visual fix with unstable temporal behavior
blindSpots: can overfit visual quality over maintainability
may prefer hardware-specific optimizations

firstClassPerspectives.name: Frontend, Interaction and Accessibility Engineering
firstClassPerspectives.reasonFirstClass: The user, browser/device, assistive technology and interaction state are part of the execution environment; correctness includes perceivability, operability and robust interaction.
firstClassPerspectives.systemBoundary: UI code, browser/device, user, assistive technologies and network
direction: test constrained devices and assistive paths
blindSpots: can overfocus presentation layer
may underweight backend/storage constraints

firstClassPerspectives.name: Compiler and Toolchain Engineering
firstClassPerspectives.reasonFirstClass: Transforms programs while preserving semantics; correctness depends on explicit intermediate representations, analysis validity and pass ordering/invalidation.
firstClassPerspectives.systemBoundary: source languages, IRs, analyses, transformations, code generation and linker/toolchain
direction: prefer typed IR over blind text edits
blindSpots: can over-abstract application intent
may optimize transform machinery over product value

firstClassPerspectives.name: Verification and Test Engineering
firstClassPerspectives.reasonFirstClass: Optimizes falsification power, observability, oracle quality and risk coverage rather than implementation throughput.
firstClassPerspectives.systemBoundary: artifact under test, test environment, oracle, fixtures and observability
direction: ask what would falsify the claim
prioritize risk not raw test count
blindSpots: can optimize detectability over implementation simplicity
testing cannot prove absence of all faults

firstClassPerspectives.name: Performance and Capacity Engineering
firstClassPerspectives.reasonFirstClass: Treats latency distributions, throughput, resource saturation and scaling behavior as explicit quantitative constraints.
firstClassPerspectives.systemBoundary: critical path, queues, compute/memory/storage/network resources and workload
direction: separate workload change from code change
blindSpots: can trade clarity for speed unnecessarily
may ignore product semantics

firstClassPerspectives.name: Safety-Critical Engineering
firstClassPerspectives.reasonFirstClass: Failure can cause physical harm or unacceptable hazards, so hazard analysis, traceability, fail-safe states and independent evidence become architectural constraints.
firstClassPerspectives.systemBoundary: software plus physical process, humans, hardware and hazard environment
blindSpots: can impose heavy process where consequence is low
may reduce iteration speed

firstClassPerspectives.name: Robotics and Control Engineering
firstClassPerspectives.reasonFirstClass: Software closes feedback loops with noisy sensors and physical actuators; stability, latency, calibration and safe physical behavior dominate.
firstClassPerspectives.systemBoundary: software, sensors, actuators, dynamics, environment and operator
blindSpots: can over-model physical dynamics for simple automation
may underweight UI/business concerns

firstClassPerspectives.name: Scientific and Numerical Computing
firstClassPerspectives.reasonFirstClass: Correctness depends on numerical stability, conditioning, error bounds, units and reproducibility—not only type/syntax correctness.
firstClassPerspectives.systemBoundary: algorithm, floating/fixed precision, data, units, solver and reference model
blindSpots: can overvalue mathematical fidelity over system integration
may assume domain models are valid

firstClassPerspectives.name: Network and Protocol Engineering
firstClassPerspectives.reasonFirstClass: Optimizes interoperable state machines over lossy, delayed, reordered and potentially hostile communication channels.
firstClassPerspectives.systemBoundary: peers, transport/network path, protocol state and intermediaries
direction: separate transport success from application commit
blindSpots: can over-engineer local IPC
may focus wire efficiency over application clarity

firstClassPerspectives.name: Build, Release and Reproducibility Engineering
firstClassPerspectives.reasonFirstClass: Treats transformation from source to shipped artifact as a provenance-sensitive system with dependency, environment and rollback invariants.
firstClassPerspectives.systemBoundary: source, build graph, dependencies, CI environment, artifacts and deployment handoff
blindSpots: can slow experimentation if applied too early
may overvalue hermeticity for disposable prototypes
